primary_metric: weighted trips bought per year by $100,000 = (average trips per $100,000 of the mode) x marginal-effectiveness factor x access weight

options.B: More Flex: spend the $100,000 on more GO Westmoreland demand-response service

reinforcement_note: Mechanical sweep of readmodel/standards_spine.json on 2026-10-28: no skill has n=0, so no uncovered skill exists for any case to claim. Thinnest skills (n<=2) considered: 'How to multiply with negative numbers' (n=2) dropped because the shipped D4 stops at an RY2025 extension (one addition) and forces no multiplication; 'How to divide with negative numbers' (n=2) IS claimed as reinforcement (n=2->3) because the D4 slope is a negative total change divided by a positive count of years; 'How to find a missing data element given the mean' (n=1) not reached (agriculture and drill sheets in the same wave claim it); 'Non-linear' (n=2) not forced, no curve is assumed. 'How to find a whole given the percent and the part' and 'How to find a missing amount in a proportion' considered and dropped: plain division reaches the same hours and trips. scenario_constructions: Teodora Quillen, the board meeting and the $100,000 are invented; the agency and every Appendix A figure are real.
The Overview's riders (dialysis, pharmacy, wheelchair user) are constructed illustrations, not WCTA customers.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Decision date: RY2024 is the latest year the board holds
modeling_assumptions.basis: Freezes every figure at one date (SPEC 5).

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Marginal cost of an added hour = that mode's average cost per hour (carried in rho)
rho_F, marginal effectiveness of an added fixed-route hour
modeling_assumptions.basis: Added hours tend to be evenings, weekends, outer branches.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing; the answer is sensitive to this value.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: rho_D, marginal effectiveness of an added van hour
modeling_assumptions.basis: Extra van hours create trips only if unmet demand exists; NTD has no denial count.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: w, access weight of one van trip in fixed-route trips
A rider's worth = 2 x 260 trips a year

sensitivity_note: SPEC 6 applies: older adults, riders with disabilities, medical-assistance patients. Facilitator note in FACILITATOR.md. People are not ranked.

deliverables.text: A build-up table, report year 2024, for both options: cost per revenue hour, trips per revenue hour, revenue hours $100,000 buys, trips carried, trips per $100,000, riders' worth, and the gap as a percent of the larger.
A break-even sheet: the fixed-route marginal-effectiveness factor at which the options tie, as a percent of today's average, and the break-even trips per revenue hour for each mode.
An access-weight statement: the student's w, its justification, the tie weight, and the choice placed on that line.
A signed-gap trend: D = vans minus fixed per $100,000 for 2022-2024, charted, with the slope of the line through 2022 and 2024, extended to RY2025.
A decision memo: A or B, the three inputs, a passenger-miles comparison, the yardstick the board should fund, and one fact that would change the choice.

appendices.title: NTD Service and Cost Data, Westmoreland County Transit Authority, Report Years 2022-2024

balance.argument_a: At plain NTD averages fixed route buys 2,698.4 trips per $100,000 vs 2,523.7 for vans (A by 6.48%), 15.70% more passenger-miles per $100,000, and the gap moved toward fixed every year.
balance.argument_b: Marginal fixed-route hours are the weakest ones, so a fixed-route effectiveness below 0.935 flips the case; a van trip serves riders with few alternatives, so an access weight above 1.069 flips it; vans won RY2022 and RY2023.
balance.margin_basis: margin = (winner - loser)/winner on weighted trips per $100,000 at rho_F = rho_D = w = 1: (2698.4 - 2523.7)/2698.4.
balance.twist_effect: RY2025: A still wins, by 5.00%; the D4 projection (-493.5) misses the actual gap (-123.6); marginal trips per added $100,000 are -168.3 (fixed) and +822.3 (vans) over one year.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: M3 is a scenario dial with no public figure (NTD reports no marginal split). The mechanical +/-50% sweep flips the verdict below about 0.935 (at -50% B wins decisively, outside the 20% cap); disclosed as the case's central fragility, so the starting-value margin is a region boundary, not a prediction.
M4 has no public figure (no denied-trip count). Flexing it down 50% makes A win decisively; up 50% flips to B. Disclosed.
M5 is a value judgment of the board. Raising it 50% makes B win decisively; lowering it 50% makes A win decisively. The answer is the student's defended triple; disclosed in FACILITATOR.md.

facilitator.twist: Report year 2025 revealed (framed as a review a year later): A still wins by 5.00%; the D4 line's -493.5 gap prediction is -123.6 in fact; marginal trips per added $100,000 are -168.3 (fixed) vs +822.3 (vans); rho per added hour -0.22 and 0.47, per dollar -0.06 and 0.33; one year of differences is a single noisy observation.
